Weapons | Monster Hunter Wilds Wiki

This page was last edited on 15 June 2026, at 09:24.
From Monster Hunter Wilds Wiki


Weapons in Monster Hunter Wilds (MHWilds) are all the main offensive equipment available in the game used in Combat. MH Wilds offers a wide range of weapon types and individual weapons for players to choose from. These weapons are a core part of the Monster Hunter series, with many weapon categories returning from previous games. Players can view all available weapons in the game, along with details on their stats, abilities, and how to obtain them. Choosing the right weapon allows players to match their preferred build and playstyle.

  • If you are looking for Artian Weapons and guides on how to craft an Artian Weapon in MHWilds, please check our Artian Weapons page.

MH WILDS - ALL WEAPON TREES

All Monster Hunter Wilds Weapons

Since the Monster Hunter series tends to work with the same formula and returning players may want to utilize some of their favorite weapons to create similar builds from previous titles. We're expecting a lot of the old Monster Hunter weapons to make a reappearance in the game. This is consistent throughout the series, with the available weapon categories from the most recent two titles, Monster Hunter World and Monster Hunter Rise, remaining pretty identical. So while the game is still in development, we can expect to see the return of most of the following Weapons:

Great Sword ♦ Sword & Shield ♦ Dual Blades ♦ Long Sword ♦ Hunting Horn ♦ Lance ♦ Gunlance ♦ Hammer ♦ Switch Axe ♦ Charge Blade ♦ Insect Glaive ♦ Bow ♦ Light Bowgun ♦ Heavy Bowgun

Recent Changes to Weapons in MH Wilds

Weapons Now Feature Unique Equipment Skills in MH Wilds

In previous entries in the Monster Hunter series, core hunt-aiding skills were primarily acquired through armor pieces, talismans, and decorations, allowing players to mix and match for personalized builds. Monster Hunter Wilds introduces an exciting evolution of this system: weapons now come equipped with built-in Equipment Skills, making them an integral part of your build strategy.

Even weapons available early in the game feature skills tailored to their weapon type, adding depth and versatility to your hunts. For instance, the Great Sword Buster Sword I comes with Critical Draw to maximize its heavy-hitting opening strikes, while Bone Blade II offers Focus for faster charge times and an Attack Boost to enhance raw power. This innovation pairs seamlessly with the new dual-weapon mechanic, which allows you to switch between two weapons mid-hunt.

Which Weapon is best for you? All 14 MH Wilds Weapons Explained!

Weapon Balance Changes based on OBT in MH Wilds

Following feedback from the Open Beta Test, weapon actions in Monster Hunter Wilds have undergone various adjustments to enhance gameplay balance and improve the overall feel of combat. These updates address player feedback, elements initially planned for the final release, and additional tweaks included in the Day 1 update.

Some of the most notable changes target specific weapons such as the Lance, Switch Axe, Insect Glaive, and Sword & Shield. These adjustments include improvements to their mechanics, damage outputs, and overall usability. For example, the team has rebalanced the damage scaling across weapon types to create a fairer experience in the endgame while ensuring that each weapon’s unique strengths are fully realized. A key example of these changes involves the Switch Axe. Feedback indicated that the "Full Release Slash," a move at the end of one of its branches, felt underwhelming compared to other final-stage moves in terms of both mechanics and damage. To address this, the cycle leading up to the attack, along with its impact and effectiveness, has been reworked to make it more rewarding.

Changes to Ranged Weapons in MH Wilds

The developer of MH:W also makes ranged weapons (Light Bowguns, Heavy Bowguns, and Bows) playstyle more smoothly, now you no longer need to expend resources for base damage sources (normal, pierce, and spread ammo). This means you don't need to worry about replenishing your supplies when you load into different areas (As long as the gauge is not empty). However, for elemental ammo, you still need to expend your resources, to encourage players to plan ahead and manage their supplies in hunting. In addition to that, ranged weapons also get a lot of new actions.

Weapon Damage Types in Monster Hunter Wilds

There are 3 Types of Damage in MH Wilds, which depend on the type of weapon and attack move that you are using. The 3 types are: Cut, Blunt, and Ammo, and helps determine the effectiveness of the damage that you are dealing to a monster. It is important to know that Monster Body Parts have Specific Body Part weakness ratings for each. This means that attacking certain body parts using certain weapon/weapon moves will yield more damage compared to another damage source. Typically, monsters have a 3- 4 ★★★★ Blunt weakness to their head, which is a great spot for attacking for Hammer users as it makes Stunning them more efficient.
  • Ammo or Projectile Damage is primarily composed of Bows, Light Bowguns, and Heavy Bowguns. This refers to weapons that require ammo to damage a monster, including the Slinger.
  • Blunt Damage is primarily composed of Hammers and Hunting Horns, but can also be inflicted through weapon attacks like Shield Bash (Sword & Shield), Arc Shot (Bows), and some Kinsect attacks.
  • Cut or Severing Damage is primarily composed of sharp weapons such as Dual Blades, Long Sword, and Switch Axe. This damage type can cut monster body parts like Tails.

The Damage types in MH Wilds is not limited to the type of weapon that the hunter is using. For example, the Bow primarily deals Ammo Damage, but it has a move called the Dragon Piercer that can cut through monster parts. It can also be used to target the base of the monster's tail to cut it off, as opposed to the usual way of hacking and slashing with Cut Damage.

Integrating Weapon Skills with the Dual Weapon System in MH Wilds

The inclusion of equipment skills on weapons is closely tied to Monster Hunter Wilds’ new dual-weapon system. Previously, skills were exclusively tied to armor, which often created challenges in optimizing builds. Players had to match armor sets to specific weapon types, which limited flexibility and often made it difficult to adapt to different playstyles or weapon switches mid-hunt.

In Monster Hunter Wilds, this issue has been addressed by attaching core skills directly to weapons. This design ensures that your main skills are always active, regardless of the armor you equip. When switching between your main and sub-weapons, these weapon-specific skills stay relevant, making your builds more adaptable.

This system allows for much greater freedom in crafting skill configurations. For instance, players can enhance weapons further by adding additional skills via accessories, unlocking even more versatility as the weapons are upgraded. It’s important to note that weapon skills are distinct and cannot occupy armor skill slots.


How Do Weapon Skills Work in Monster Hunter Wilds

Weapon Skills are abilities built directly into weapons and play an important role in creating a hunter's build.

Unlike previous titles, where many essential combat skills were gained through armor, talismans, and decorations, Monster Hunter Wilds allows weapons to provide their own Equipment Skills. These skills can enhance specific aspects of combat, such as improving certain attack styles or increasing overall effectiveness.

Since Weapon Skills are tied to the equipped weapon, selecting a weapon is not only about its damage or elemental properties. The skills it provides can also influence your overall strategy.

Adjustments to the Insect Glaive in MH Wilds

In Monster Hunter Wilds, the Insect Glaive’s playstyle has shifted to emphasize ground-based combat rather than the aerial dominance seen in Monster Hunter World: Iceborne. While this adjustment was intentional, it sparked significant feedback from players who valued the weapon's traditional airborne identity.

One notable change involved the "Vaulting Dance" move, a signature aerial action from previous titles. Initially absent from the demo, this omission was part of a deliberate design choice to shift the focus away from aerial damage-dealing and highlight new ground-based mechanics. The developers seem to want to encourage players to explore the Insect Glaive's new moves by removing this from the demo and this decision was intended to shift the focus toward the weapon's updated combat style and capabilities. However, feedback from Insect Glaive enthusiasts expressed that "Vaulting Dance" was more than just a gameplay feature, it was a defining aspect of the weapon’s identity.

In response, the development team has reinstated "Vaulting Dance" in the current adjustments, balancing it to ensure it complements the new mechanics rather than overshadowing them.

What are Layered Weapons in MH Wilds

Layered Weapons allow hunters to change the appearance of their weapon without changing its stats, damage, or skills. Once you craft the final weapon in a weapon tree, you can unlock its appearance as a layered weapon and apply that design to other weapons.

This lets you customize your hunter's style while still using the weapon that best suits your build. High Rank Palico weapons can also be unlocked as layered equipment for your Felyne companion. Some weapons that change appearance as they are upgraded will also make their earlier designs available as layered options. For Artian Weapons, their layered appearances can be unlocked by fully reinforcing a Rarity 8 Artian Weapon.

This system gives players more freedom to create their preferred look without sacrificing performance in the game.


Combat Innovations in Monster Hunter Wilds

The recent State of Play trailer for Monster Hunter Wilds introduced several exciting new features that promise to enhance the gameplay experience. These innovations focus on improving mobility, adding dynamic combat options, and integrating environmental interactions more deeply into the hunting experience.

Sprinting with Weapons

Great Sword Running: For the first time in the mainline series, hunters can sprint with their great sword unsheathed. This feature allows for more fluid movement and dynamic positioning during hunts. By enabling faster, more aggressive gameplay, hunters can reduce downtime between attacks and improve their mobility while maintaining an offensive stance.

Slide-Grinding Attacks

Hunters can now perform slide-grinding attacks where the weapon is dragged along the monster's body, dealing continuous damage. This move allows for sustained damage over a larger surface area, making it particularly effective against massive monsters. In the trailer, a hunter is seen using this move with a great sword, sliding along the monster's body and causing multiple damage ticks.

Mounted Combat

On-the-Go Attacks: Hunters can perform attacks while riding their mounts. This includes basic attacks as well as potentially more complex moves, depending on the mount and weapon combination. Mounted combat enables quick repositioning, allowing hunters to avoid damage, close distances rapidly, and maintain pressure on the monster.

Special dismounting attacks provide additional opportunities to damage monsters as hunters transition from mounted to ground combat. This feature enhances the fluidity and dynamism of hunts, offering new strategic options.

Dynamic Environment Interactions

Environmental Hazards: Weather changes, like sandstorms, significantly affect visibility and monster behavior. Hunters must adapt their strategies to these dynamic conditions, adding another layer of challenge and realism to the game.

Swapping Mechanics in Monster Hunter Wilds

One of the most exciting innovations in Monster Hunter Wilds is the introduction of a dual weapon system, allowing hunters to bring two different weapons into a hunt and swap between them as needed. This new mechanic offers significant tactical flexibility, enabling hunters to adapt to different phases of a hunt or various types of monsters they may encounter.

Dynamic Combat Approach

The ability to swap weapons mid-hunt transforms the hunter's approach to combat. This mechanic allows hunters to dynamically change their strategy based on the monster's behavior, the environment, and their current needs. For example, a hunter might begin with a great sword to deliver powerful blows and stagger the monster, then switch to a bowgun for a more defensive, ranged approach as the monster becomes more aggressive or when maintaining distance is advantageous.

Dual Weapon System

The dual weapon system means that hunters no longer need to commit to a single weapon for the entire duration of a hunt. Instead, they can dynamically switch between two chosen weapons. This allows for a strategic adaptation, such as starting a fight with a heavy-hitting weapon like a great sword to break monster parts, then switching to a bowgun for safer, ranged damage as the monster becomes enraged.

How Does the Dual Weapon System Work?

The Dual Weapon System allows hunters to carry two different weapons during a hunt and swap between them whenever needed.

This creates more flexibility in combat. A hunter may use a heavy weapon to capitalize on openings and then switch to a ranged weapon when a monster becomes difficult to approach. Weapon swapping can also be performed while riding a Seikret, allowing hunters to adapt without disrupting the flow of battle

On-Mount Swapping

Swapping weapons is made even more seamless with the ability to do so while riding mounts. This integration ensures that the process is smooth and does not interrupt the flow of combat. Hunters can quickly switch their weapons without needing to dismount, maintaining their momentum and tactical advantage.
